And are not his sisters here with us?’ And they took offense at him.”

A little later it is added: “And he could perform no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them; and he marveled because of their unbelief.”

What does this mean, brothers? Paul affirms that signs were given for unbelievers, while Mark asserts that they were withheld because of unbelievers. Can those who are filled with one Spirit present mutually contradictory opinions?

We must observe, however, that there was a certain difference among the unbelievers themselves. The error of all who did not believe was alike, but their merits differed greatly. It is one thing for someone to be deceived by ignorance alone, and another for wickedness also to be added.

Paul sinned through ignorance, for he said: “I was formerly a blasphemer and a persecutor and an insolent man, but I obtained mercy because I acted in ignorance.” Judas sinned through wickedness, and therefore did not merit to come to forgiveness.

Signs were therefore given for those unbelievers whom divine providence had mercifully determined to save; but they were withheld because of those whom, on account of their merits, the justice of strict severity excluded from the company of the elect.

### II. In a Letter to Abbot Desiderius, Where He Discusses the Restoration of a Virgin

*(Ed. vol. III, p. 613.)*

“When he has handed over the kingdom to God the Father.”

According to the sound of the words, this seems in a certain way to signify that, so long as the Son held the kingdom, the Father did not possess it, and that, when he hands it over to the Father, he himself no longer holds it.

Yet to hand over the kingdom to God the Father, according to a sober understanding, means nothing other than to lead believers to contemplate the appearance of God the Father. The kingdom is then handed over by the Son to God the Father when, through the Mediator between God and human beings, the multitude of the faithful is transferred into contemplation of the eternal divinity—that is, when the dispensation of likenesses through angels, principalities, powers, and virtues is no longer necessary.

Speaking in their person, it is fittingly understood that the bride is told in the Song of Songs: “We will make for you likenesses of gold with settings of silver, until the king is in his retreat.” That is, until Christ is in his secret place, because “your life is hidden with Christ in God.” “When Christ,” he says, “who is your life appears, then you also will appear with him in glory.”

Before this takes place, “we now see through a mirror in an enigma”—that is, in likenesses—“but then face to face.” This contemplation is promised to us as the end of all actions and the eternal perfection of joys. For we are children, and it has not yet appeared what we shall be; we know that when he appears, we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is.

He says: “This is eternal life: that they should know you, the one true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” This will happen when the Lord comes and “brings to light the things hidden in darkness.” When the darkness of this mortality and corruption has passed, then our morning will come—the morning of which the Psalm says: “In the morning I will stand before you and see.”

It is of this contemplation that the words “when he has handed over the kingdom to God the Father” are understood: that is, when the Mediator between God and human beings, the man Christ Jesus, leads to the contemplation of God the Father the righteous, in whom he now reigns as they live by faith.

### III. In a Letter to Peter the Monk

*(Ed. vol. I, p. 219.)*

Paul boasts that he was beaten with rods three times and that five times he received forty lashes less one. Moses had commanded that anyone whom the judges deemed deserving of blows should be beaten according to the measure of his sin, but in such a way that they did not exceed the number forty.

The number forty signifies the course of human life. The prohibition against exceeding that number while someone is being beaten signifies that whoever has performed perfect penance in this life will afterward feel no punishment for his transgressions.

The number three, because of the mystery of the Holy Trinity, pertains to faith; the number five, because of our five senses, pertains to action. Since Paul had sinned in both respects—erring in faith and offending in action—it was fitting that he should be beaten three times with rods and five times with forty lashes, for the work of complete purification.

As for the phrase “one less,” this undoubtedly refers to the fact that the Jewish judges decreed that one stroke should be subtracted from forty, so that, while they did not reach the legal number, they could in no way exceed the command of the Law; and while they remained short of it, they would not pass beyond it. [The transmitted reading *eitra* is evidently uncertain; the sense requires “short of it” or “within the limit.”]

## FROM THE LETTERS TO TIMOTHY

### I. In a Letter to Cardinal Bishops on the Dignity of the Roman Church

*(Ed. vol. I, p. 51.)*

“Whoever desires the office of bishop desires a good work.”

This plainly shows that a pontiff is nothing other than a pursuer of good work. For he did not say, “He desires a good dignity” or “He desires a good honor,” but, “Whoever desires the office of bishop desires a good work.” It is as though he were saying: Whoever longs to possess the episcopate without good work wishes to assume an empty name without the reality of the office itself.

The episcopate, therefore, does not consist in the ornaments of flowing ribbons, nor finally in the masses of tightly packed ranks of soldiers, but in uprightness of conduct and the practice of holy virtues.

He immediately adds: “It is necessary for a bishop to be blameless.” Here the Apostle requires a bishop to possess such perfection that he seems almost to be speaking beyond the limits of human nature. For who, living in the flesh, will live so cautiously and look around himself so diligently on every side that he can never be criticized?

Woe to those who live blameworthy lives and, even more blameworthily, desire a position in which they may live blamelessly! Among these are those who, forgetting affection for kinship and homeland, follow the camps of kings through unknown and barbarous kingdoms of the earth. The ambition for perishing dignities drives them to this—an ambition that the promise of heavenly rewards could not compel.

### II. In a Letter to V. the Bishop, Where the Letter of Transmundi Is Mentioned, Said to Have Been Sealed with This Bishop’s Seal

*[Note: Some letters of Saint Peter Damian, and also certain brief works addressed to V., the bishop, are extant; yet this lengthy passage, unless I am mistaken, is not found in them. It therefore seems to have been taken from another letter to the same man, one that is no longer extant. Although this passage does not appear to belong to the collections from the New Testament, I nevertheless gladly publish it, both because it is written continuously in the manuscript and because it contains a doctrine concerning unleavened bread suitable for explaining the holy doctor’s statement in his exposition of the Canon, where he said that Peter defends the position of the Latin Church concerning unleavened bread against the Greeks, who, as controversialists demonstrate, prefer leavened bread to unleavened on the basis not of dogma but of an erroneous historical claim. Here, however, Peter rightly asserts the value of both kinds. Nor does the letter of Saint Peter Damian to Buccon, which we append, appear to be found in his published works.]*

## Whether Leavened Bread May Be Offered

In a letter to Henry, archbishop of Ravenna.

Just as it makes no difference in the sacrifice whether we offer wine or must, so, as it seems to me, it is the same whether one offers leavened bread or unleavened. For that living bread which descended from heaven wished to signify itself not only through the kind of grain but likewise through the vine.

“Unless,” he says, “a grain of wheat falling into the ground dies, it remains alone.” And again: “I am the true vine.”

Let it therefore be enough for me simply to offer either what is made from grain or what is produced from the vine. I do not anxiously investigate whether the bread was kept raw in the dough until it could ferment, or whether the must was stored in a *timna* [term uncertain] until it could pass into the designation of wine. But since it is not our purpose here to dispute these matters, we leave them for others to discuss.

## Peter to His Very Dear Son Buccon

Your affection led you to consult me as to whether the angels through whom almighty God strikes the sins of sinners and is accustomed to inflict punishment, whether by sudden death or by some other misfortune, are good or evil angels.

The answer is plainly easy and clear. For if Holy Scripture is carefully examined, vengeance is found to be carried out through both kinds of spirits, according to the decree of the supreme Judge.

To keep a concise statement from lingering over an evident matter: Sodom was destroyed by good angels. For if they had been hostile powers, blessed Lot would neither have worshiped them nor reverently received them as guests, as we read: “I beg you, my lords, turn aside into the house of your servant and stay there.”

The angel who struck seventy thousand men while David was numbering the people was likewise unquestionably good. Scripture reports concerning him: “The angel of the Lord commanded Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the Lord God on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.” For a rejected spirit would not have commanded the Prophet to build an altar, nor would the Prophet have devoutly obeyed him with humility.

Those angels were also holy who, as the Second Book of Maccabees says, struck Heliodorus when he attempted to remove money from the holy temple and, afflicting him with terrifying blows and striking him with blindness, left him as though dead.

Concerning them Scripture continues: “There appeared to them a certain horse with a terrible rider, adorned with the finest trappings. It rushed upon Heliodorus and struck him with its front hooves; the one sitting upon it appeared to have golden armor. Two other young men also appeared, remarkable in strength, excellent in glory, and beautiful in attire. They stood on either side of him and scourged him without ceasing, beating him with many blows. Suddenly Heliodorus fell to the ground; they seized him, surrounded by deep darkness, placed him upon a litter, and carried him away.”

That God also inflicts his scourges upon human beings through rejected spirits is frequently made clear by Scripture. An evil spirit had invaded King Saul and tormented him with mad fury. Satan struck blessed Job not only in his body but also by depriving him of his children. The demon Asmodeus, as the sequence of the sacred history relates, killed the seven husbands of Sarah, daughter of Raguel.

Hence it is written: “He sent among them indignation, anger, and troubles through evil angels.”

It is therefore established that through both kinds of angels—good and evil—God avenges the movements of divine justice against us, as is proved by these and many other testimonies of sacred discourse.

But since all such acts of vengeance and punishment are administered by angelic service according to the divine sentence, it lies solely within the judgment of almighty God whether they occur through good angels or through evil ones.

To avoid wandering through distant examples: blessed Cecilia was threatened with the fury of a good angel, while blessed Agnes the martyr declares that vengeance was carried out by an evil angel.

Cecilia announced to her betrothed Valerian: “I have an angel of God as my lover, who guards my body with excessive zeal. If he senses even slightly that you touch me with polluted love, he will immediately stir up his fury against you, and you will lose the flower of your most pleasing youth.”

Agnes, however, says to the prefect concerning his son, who had been strangled by an evil spirit: “The one whose will he wanted to fulfill himself received power over him.”

The authority of both the New and the Old Testament therefore clearly establishes that divine punishment is administered not only through evil angels but also through good angels. A householder, after all, both captures wild beasts and drives out thieves—sometimes through puppies, sometimes through household servants.

# FRAGMENTS

## Notice Concerning the Following Fragment and Letter of May

The following fragment does not occur in the published letter of blessed Peter Damian to Henry, archbishop of Ravenna, nor in the brief work addressed to the same man—unless my eye has perhaps gone astray. It therefore seems to have been taken from another letter to the same person that is no longer extant.

Although this passage does not appear to belong to the collections from the New Testament, I nevertheless gladly publish it, both because it is written continuously in the manuscript and because it contains a doctrine concerning unleavened bread suitable for explaining the holy doctor’s statement, which he made in no. 2 of his exposition of the Canon.

There Peter defends the position of the Latin Church concerning unleavened bread against the Greeks, who, as controversialists demonstrate, prefer leavened bread to unleavened on the basis not of dogma but of an erroneous historical claim. Here, however, Peter rightly asserts the value of both kinds.

Nor does the letter of Saint Peter Damian to Buccon, which we append, appear to occur in his published works.

# THE FOURTH VOLUME OF THE WORKS OF SAINT PETER DAMIAN IN THE CAJETAN EDITION, CONTAINING SACRED POEMS AND PRAYERS

## The Privilege of Pope Paul V

Pope Paul V to his beloved son Constantine Cajetan, of Syracuse, monk of Saint Nicholas of the Arena at Catania, of the Cassinese Congregation of the Order of Saint Benedict.

Beloved son, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since, as we have learned, you are about to publish the works of the blessed Peter Damian, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and bishop of Ostia—works which, not without detriment to ecclesiastical letters, had lain scattered in various places in darkness, and which through your praiseworthy work, labor, and diligence, together with numerous other monuments of ecclesiastical writers, have been sought out and collected from many libraries—and since for this reason our predecessor, Clement VIII of happy memory, moved by his zeal to serve the Christian commonwealth and the Apostolic See, of which this distinguished doctor had been a noble member, had summoned you to Rome; now, since by divine grace the first volume has been completed and you hope shortly to publish the remaining three, we, who are bound by pastoral charity to embrace the learned studies of pious and erudite men and ardently desire such undertakings to be advanced in the Lord, wish that both the first volume of these works, already printed, and the others when they are printed, may appear genuine and corrected, and that they may not be adulterated or damaged through anyone’s negligence or fraud.

Therefore, by our own motion and from certain knowledge, by apostolic authority and through these presents, we forbid and prohibit all and each of the faithful of Christ, especially printers of books and booksellers of whatever name, both in the City and throughout the territories and places mediately or immediately subject to the Holy Roman Church, under penalty of a fine of five hundred gold ducats, to be applied to the Apostolic Camera, as well as the loss of the books and type; and all persons anywhere in Italy and outside it, wherever they may be, under penalty of automatic major excommunication, incurred by the very fact without any further declaration:

They must not dare or presume, for fifteen years reckoned from the date of these presents, to print without your permission the first volume of the works of the blessed Peter Damian published by you, or any of the others to be published by you—provided that all have been approved by the Master of the Sacred Palace—for the same number of years reckoned from the publication of each individual volume; nor, under any pretext, to publish them altered under another title or in another form, or translated into any other language, nor to sell books so published or keep them for sale.

We command all and each of our venerable brothers, patriarchs, archbishops, bishops and other local ordinaries, legates, vice-legates, governors, magistrates, and other officials, whenever and as often as they are requested by you or in your name, to enforce the foregoing against the disobedient and to cause it to be observed, invoking for this purpose, if necessary, the aid of the secular arm.

Notwithstanding apostolic constitutions and ordinances, statutes and customs strengthened by oath, apostolic confirmation, or any other authority; and also notwithstanding privileges, indults, and apostolic letters granted and confirmed in whatever manner to any persons. Although we hold all their contents as expressly included in these presents as if they had been inserted word for word, for this occasion only we derogate from them, and from all other contrary provisions.

We wish that copies of these letters, even when printed in the volumes themselves, should everywhere receive the same authority as these presents would receive if they had been produced or shown.

Given at Rome, at Saint Mark’s, under the Fisherman’s Ring, on 17 August 1606, in the second year of our pontificate.

Scipio Cobellutius.

[Col. 0913]

## Eulogy of Saint Peter Damian

[Col. 0913A] Bernard, or rather Berthold, a priest of Constance, in the book *On Avoiding Communion with the Excommunicated*:

Peter Damian, of blessed memory, cardinal bishop of the holy Roman Church, was another Jerome in our time.

So says Bernard, who also brings forward the same testimony in chapter 10 of his other book, *Decrees*, in a manuscript preserved among us. The most eminent Cardinal Baronius, likewise led by the authority of the ancient writers, was accustomed to address this distinguished doctor of ours as “the Younger Jerome.”

[Col. 0913]

## On the Feast Day of Saint Peter Damian  
### A Preliminary Notice by the Lord Constantine Cajetan

[Col. 0913B] The feast day of Saint Peter Damian has been celebrated every year with solemn observance from time immemorial, both at Ravenna and in all the other cities and places of the region of Flaminia whose churches are subject to the metropolitan Church of Ravenna. Accordingly, each year the same distinguished doctor is also listed by the prelates of those cities, among the other saints enrolled in the Calendar of heavenly spirits, in the printed Order of the Divine Office.

It is there recorded as follows:

*Calendar of the holy metropolitan archiepiscopal Church of Ravenna and its diocese, published by order of the most eminent and reverend lord, Lord Aloysius Capponius, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and archbishop of that same holy Church of Ravenna.*

In the same Calendar, under the twenty-third day of February, the following is prescribed:

[Col. 0913C] Peter Damian, bishop and confessor of Ravenna: double feast; yesterday was observed. At the first nocturn: “Let us praise.” At the second nocturn: “Of the blessed Father,” as in the Common of Confessors who are Pontiffs. At the third nocturn: “Watch,” as in the same Common; ninth lesson, and commemoration of the feria. Prayer for the saint: “Hear us.” Vespers from the preceding day, with commemoration of the following day.

To this may be added the Calendar of the Church of Faenza, in these words:

*Order of the Divine Office to be recited and Masses to be celebrated according to the rite of the Roman Breviary and Missal, in the Church and diocese of Faenza, published by order of the most eminent lord, Lord Francis, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church, of the title of Saint Marcellus, bishop of that same city.*

And in it, under the same day as above, the twenty-third of February, the following is also prescribed:

[Col. 0914B] Peter Damian, bishop and confessor, and protector of Faenza: greater double feast.

Lessons of the first nocturn: “A faithful saying.” Of the second: “Of the blessed Father.” Of the third: “Watch,” with the other material from the Common of Confessors who are Pontiffs. Ninth lesson: homily and commemoration of the feria. In the office nothing is done concerning the vigil of Saint Matthias. White vestments.

Mass: “Priests.” Second prayer: of the feria, whose Gospel is read at the end. Third prayer: of the vigil of Saint Matthias. Preface of Lent. At second Vespers, commemoration of the feria. A procession is held in the city by vow.

These matters from the Churches of Ravenna and Faenza—and likewise from the Calendars of the churches of the rest of the same province, which for the sake of brevity we now pass over—show the divine honors freely offered to Peter Damian, both in the ecclesiastical office and in the most holy sacrifice of the Mass, from a time whose memory does not exist. There can be no doubt that this was done with the authority of the Roman Pontiff. Concerning this, it is entirely proper and worthwhile to conclude that Peter Damian was enrolled among the number of the saints by that same Roman Pontiff: first from what we have just said, then from other evidence that we cited at the beginning of the third volume of the works of this distinguished doctor, and finally from many other arguments that we can bring forward on the same matter.

[Col. 0913]

## Notable Testimonies concerning the Commendable Exertion Undertaken by Lord Abbot Constantine Cajetan on the Works of Saint Peter Damian

Caesar Baronius, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, librarian of the Apostolic See, *Ecclesiastical Annals*, volume 11, under the year of Christ 1072.

[Col. 0913D]

Thus, in this most deplorable age, when a flood of the flesh had grown so great as to overwhelm the Church, God gave the world such a man that by the example of his most austere life, and by preaching and writing, he might dry up so great a corruption, and at the same time fight against the simoniacal heresy, which was spreading with impunity everywhere.

As for his writings, we do not delay here to list them all, since at present, in the year 1604, the Lord Dom Constantine Cajetan, a Sicilian monk of the Cassinese Congregation, is laboring by command of our most blessed lord Clement, the eighth pope, to gather the monuments of this most holy man’s writings from every quarter and commit them to the press; and I hope this will happen shortly. For he is working with great zeal and unwearied effort to investigate them and to correct the many copies brought from various places. From him you will also receive a fuller account of the life of Peter himself.

Robert Bellarmine, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mary in Via, in his book *On Ecclesiastical Writers*, under the year of Christ 1660.

Peter Damian—so called from the name of his brother Damian—was from Ravenna, a monk of the Order of Saint Benedict, and afterward a cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and bishop of Ostia. He lived during the time of Gregory VI and his successors up to Gregory VII, to all of whom he wrote letters. He was a very holy and devout man, and an especially ardent lover of penance and an austere life.

A little later:

He died while serving as an apostolic legate, in the year of the Lord 1072. He wrote very many letters and a great many sermons. These two works were recently committed to print at Rome, in the years 1606 and 1608, by the Lord Dom Constantine Cajetan, a monk of the Order of Saint Benedict.

[Col. 0915]

## Letter of Constantine Cajetan to the Lords Francis and Anthony Barberini, Princes

He asks that, under their patronage, his book be offered to the Supreme Pontiff.

[Col. 0915B] To the sons of the brother of our most holy lord Urban VIII, the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, Lord Francis, vice-chancellor of the Apostolic See and protector of the Roman and Apostolic Gregorian College, and Lord Anthony, chamberlain of the Holy Roman Church and prefect of both Signatures and of the Sacred Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith, princes Barberini: Dom Constantine Cajetan, abbot, sends greetings and happiness.

The fourth volume of the books of Saint Peter Damian, cardinal and bishop of Ostia, now being published, presents itself to you, most eminent cardinals, so that through you it may be offered to your uncle, the most holy Lord Urban VIII. For no one adequately understands the height and greatness of supreme power among human beings who dares to burst in upon it uninvited and without a guide.

Although the book itself, by the name of its author—a man most distinguished for learning and holiness—and by the weight and usefulness of the matters contained in it, will in itself be sufficiently welcome to one who is a patron of learning and an advocate of holiness, it nevertheless hopes to receive some additional commendation and favor from the splendor of both your names and the greatness of your authority. Thus, with you leading the way, it may appear more eagerly and confidently before the presence of the greatest Pontiff.

May the good and great God preserve you safe for a very long time, for the benefit of his Church.

[Col. 0915]

## Cajetan’s Dedicatory Letter to Pope Urban VIII

[Col. 0915C] To our holy lord Urban VIII, supreme pontiff: Constantine Cajetan, abbot, wishes everlasting happiness.

The fourth and now final volume of the works of the blessed Peter Damian, cardinal and bishop of Ostia, is being made public, most blessed Father. Nevertheless, it shows the reverence customary before so great a majesty: it did not dare to come forth into public view before humbly venerating Urban seated on the chair of Peter.

Surely, I believe, no one will fail to praise this greatly. For where could the offspring of noble minds more happily receive the beginnings of light than in the inner chambers of the Apostolic See? In those inner chambers from which the voice that will cleanse the nations from their crimes is sent forth; where the mysteries of the heavenly oracle are revealed; where the gifts of the everlasting treasure are distributed; and where, finally, the antidote of death and the medicine of life are administered.

What name could be placed more gloriously at the head of pages destined, so to speak, to survive than the name that resounds in the mouths of peoples, adorns public monuments, dignifies private ornaments, and is pronounced by the voice of priests amid the most sacred mysteries?

Who would not hope that, with the light of so august a star leading the way, all storms and all monsters hostile to voyagers would easily give way, until victorious devotion in labor and courage triumphant over dangers should bring them to the harbor of blessed life, which the boundless goodness and omnipotent wisdom of our Creator has prepared for those who live piously?

But these things would more properly be said in the books of others, who have newly and recently come under the protection of the Apostolic See. For the distinguished Benedictine doctor Peter Damian’s extraordinary fidelity and almost singular devotion toward the Roman Church need no commendation from me. His writings—of which people now enjoy a very large part through the commands of the supreme Pontiffs Clement VIII and Paul V—and the notable deeds of his life and accomplishments have remained sufficiently known and attested to posterity, so much so that he was deservedly called by the illustrious men of his age “another Jerome.”

Indeed, that most holy man did not degenerate from his forebears—I mean the fathers of the Benedictine Order—whose studies, labors, vigils, and outstanding virtue in every form of praise have brought such abundant fruits to the Christian commonwealth in every age. I might perhaps recall them here at some length, were they not recorded in public monuments, so that their memory will remain in blessing among all posterity.

For the whole Church of the saints is filled not only with the examples but also with the traces of the most beautiful works accomplished by the great patriarch Benedict and his disciples for the glory of Christ and the common good of humanity.

For this reason I consider it right and consistent with reason that I, who profess the same religious order, should strive with all my strength to display a comparable ardor of obedience and devotion toward the Roman Church, the chief and mother of all other churches.

For while it is shameful for everyone to degenerate from the virtue of his ancestors, this should be more disgraceful than any other fault for those who have chosen to complete the course of a glorious contest in devotion to the holy religion. The swiftest path to victory is set before them: never to look backward, nor to imitate the weariness of those who falter in the middle, but steadfastly to cling to the footsteps of those who lead bravely.

Domestic examples of my ancestors, from whom I derive my origin in the world, can also add, so to speak, torches and goads to urge me to run well. But why recount ancient matters, and those which I share with others, when I have singular affection and particular causes of reverence toward the Roman Pontiff?

For your beneficence, most blessed Father, which has bestowed on me the privilege of serving you after those great and excellent Pontiffs who preceded you—Clement VIII, Leo XI, Paul V, and Gregory XV, in whose service I labored upon the monuments of sacred letters—rightly demands and requires that I devote my entire self, in accordance with your greatness, honor, and dignity, and direct all my studies, cares, and thoughts toward the glory and esteem of this most holy See.

I will not hesitate to add only this. Just as your Holiness was previously able to recognize clearly in me a testimony of the devotion and reverence shown toward the Apostolic See both by my order and by my ancestors, so, if life is granted me and the breeze of that extraordinary kindness of yours continues to blow upon me—as it now does—you will hereafter recognize it more and more.

Meanwhile, receive with cheerful countenance this final volume of that once illustrious and most holy cardinal bishop, Peter Damian—the volume which, with God’s favor, I have now rescued from darkness and oblivion, together with three others, and which through your favor is enjoying the light of public day—and embrace it with the kindness you customarily show.

May almighty God preserve your Holiness safe and flourishing for a long time, for the sanctity of the Christian commonwealth, and may he make all its prayers and undertakings fruitful.

[Col. 0917]

# Sacred Poems and Prayers of the Blessed Peter Damian, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church

*(G)*

## 1–2. I. Prayer to God the Father

[Col. 0917D]

I beg you, boundless Mercy, almighty God the Father: do not destroy me, your creature, formed in your likeness and redeemed by the holy blood of your Son, my Lord Jesus Christ.

Stretch out your hand to me, Lord my God, and rescue me from the deepest pit of my iniquities. Raise me when I have fallen; release me from my chains; enlighten me who am blind; heal me, wounded by a thousand blows from evil spirits.

Alas for me, miserable man! Alas for me, ruined man! Alas for me, deserving of mourning with an unfailing fountain of tears! While I lived according to the laws of my most filthy flesh, I never allowed you to rejoice over me, but continually provoked you to bitterness by the crimes of my rejected life.

Yet I know, Lord, that everything rests upon your will, and that no one can resist your will (Esther XIII). For if you determine to save us, we shall immediately be freed.

[Col. 0918D] Bring forth, Lord, from the stony hardness of my heart an abundance of tears—you who commanded a most generous stream of flowing water to issue from the rock in the wilderness (Exodus XVII; Numbers XX; Psalm LXXVII).

Lord Jesus Christ, if you are the true light and I worship you, why do you allow me to remain in darkness? Woe is me: I adore the light and endure darkness; I serve the truth and am deceived by the fabrications of empty thoughts.

Lord, who illuminated the caverns of Tartarus with the rays of your divinity; who drove away the dense darkness of Egypt through the prayers of your servant Moses (Exodus X): look upon this chaos and flood the dark hell of my heart with the light of your visitation, so that the author of darkness may not possess in the gloom of his obscurity the soul which you, eternal Light, have deigned to redeem.

You who enlightened the man blind from birth, enlighten me (John IX). You who cleansed lepers, purify me. You who raised Lazarus from the tomb, raise me, foul with vices and weighed down by the burden of perverse habit (John XI).

You who protected Daniel in the den from the lions’ bites, rescue me (Daniel, final chapter). You who freed the three young men from the fire of the blazing furnace, free me (Daniel III). You who freed Israel from the oppression of Pharaoh, free me (Exodus XII and XIII). You who freed David from the hands of Goliath and Saul, free me (1 Samuel XVI). You who led Peter out of Herod’s prison, free me (Acts XII).

Blessed, glorious, most merciful Lord, you see—and you yourself are witness to my conscience—that I wish to reject all my evils and obey your holy commands, as is fitting; but because I cannot do so by myself, I hope in you.

For I do not find anything good in my flesh. And truly, Lord, who among the saints has ever been able by himself to possess virtue or holiness? Who has climbed to the summit of perfection by his own power, without assistance?

Certainly, Lord, neither Peter nor Paul, neither martyr nor apostle, nor even the angels themselves, neither cherubim nor seraphim, could have possessed any gift unless they had received it from you.

If, then, the very powers of heaven have nothing from themselves, but have received everything from you, what good can you expect from me, who am dung and a worm, dust and ashes, except what you yourself deign to pour into me?

For you are the Father of lights, from whom every good gift and every perfect gift comes (James I). You are the one from whom all good things proceed. You are the fountain of life. You are the author of eternal salvation.

Just as light is always poured upon the earth not from the earth itself but from heaven, so my soul, like earth without water before you (Psalm CXLII), always lies dark, filthy, and dry, unless it is drenched with the dew of your grace and illuminated by the ray of your splendor.

Indeed, Lord, I search within myself for something to offer you, but when I turn over all the secrets of my heart, I see nothing there but darkness; I find absolutely nothing but the thistles and thorns of vices.

Look, then, Lord, upon my misery; look upon the poverty of such destitution, and grant me the grace of compunction, which can wipe away the rust of my soul and wash away the stains, red with blood, of my crimes.

Drive, Lord, this coldness and torpor from my breast, and kindle in me the flame of your sweetest charity.

For surely, Lord, can my iniquity overcome the immense abundance of your mercy, which the crimes of the whole world could not overcome?

[Col. 0919D] For when nearly the whole world was devoted to idolatry, who would have dared to ask you to visit the narrow confines of a virgin’s womb—to dwell there, you whom the heavens cannot contain—and to assume the members of our mortality and endure the torments of the most terrible death, so that you might free your enemies from the punishment due to death?

If, therefore, most merciful and most loving Lord, the sins of the whole world did not overcome the greatness of your mercy, will the sins of one dead dog, however grave, overcome it? Far be this from you, Lord. Far be it from you, who said: “I do not desire the death of the sinner” (Ezekiel XVIII, XXXIII).

What then is the meaning of what you say: “There is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents”? (Luke XV.) What is the meaning of what the Prophet says concerning you: “For your mercies are above all your works”? (Psalm CXLIV.)

Did you not, Lord, allow yourself to be touched by that most filthy and shameful woman who was stained by a bloody flow? (Matthew IX; Luke VIII.) You not only did not condemn the boldness of her presumption in any way, but even allowed her to seize salvation together with the fringe of your garment.

Did you not, most gentle Lord, deign to speak with that woman of Samaria who had had many husbands? (John IV.) Or, greater still, did you not converse with the Canaanite woman who worshiped idols? (Matthew XV.) Moreover, you freed her daughter from the demon through her mother’s prayers.

Show me, I beg you, Lord, this rule of your wondrous mercy toward me; rekindle the extinguished spark of my unhappy soul with these kindling drops of your oil.

I do not seek the mercy shown to Paul or Peter, because while one sinned through ignorance and the other through fear, each easily obtained pardon.

Grant me, most merciful Lord, that form of your mercy; offer to my sick—or rather now dying—soul the cup of your sweetest medicine which you mercifully offered to the thief hanging on the cross, and drew him, already swallowed, from the jaws of devouring death (Luke XXIII).

I seek that kind of your mercy which you extended to the woman caught in adultery (John VIII), which you bestowed upon the sinful woman in Simon’s house (Luke VII), who, while wiping your feet with her hair, cleansed her soul from the filth of sins.

In this way draw me to yourself, my Savior; kindle me; purify me. Let all my inward parts be filled with your love, so that my soul may bless you and your mercy may descend upon me.

For the almighty Father sent you into the world for this purpose: to save sinners—you who, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, live and reign as God forever and ever. Amen.

## II. Prayer to God the Son

Remember, Lord Jesus Christ, that you redeemed me not with gold or silver but at the price of your own blood (1 Peter I). Since you are the open fountain of the house of David for the cleansing of the sinner and the menstruating woman, will I alone, Lord, be deprived of such mercy and remain outside the line of your redemption?

Alas, most merciful Lord, will you allow me, together with the garment of your regeneration which you gave me and the banner of the holy cross which you painted upon my forehead, to fall into the hands of the devil and to be tortured with those same signs of yours in eternal fires?

I know, Lord, that you are so merciful that, if I turn perfectly to you, you will immediately receive me. But because I am so weak and ignorant that this conversion cannot rightly take place through me without you, convert me, God my Savior; enlighten my soul; direct me; kindle in me the flame of your love.

And perhaps, most just and most merciful Lord, my sins are so great [Note: [Col. 0919D] This means that our works cannot make satisfaction by the powers of nature; for, once God’s grace and [Col. 0920D] acceptance are presupposed, they do make satisfaction, as theologians teach at greater length.] that none of my repentance is sufficient to mourn them.

Behold my body, through which I, wretched man, offended you. You who are the physician of souls, strike it, scourge it, lash it. Whether with leprosy or with whatever pains may seem right to you, strike it most severely.

I am plainly your creature, my Creator. Bind me with your scourges, and do not hand me over to the hands of my enemy. Or, if my iniquity has advanced so far that it cannot be erased in this life, command that I be afflicted with avenging punishments until the day of your judgment, so that then at least I may deserve to be found among the last of all your elect.

Far be it from me to ask for glory. It is enough for me merely to escape punishment.

But since my prayers, uttered by such a filthy mouth, do not deserve to rise to you, I beg you, blessed Virgin Mary, temple of the living God, hall of the eternal King, sanctuary of the Holy Spirit, blessed among women:

The field of your most sacred womb gives off a fragrance to the nostrils of my heart. From that field, when that one and unique lily sprang forth, every seedling of spiritual virtues burst forth together with it.

For you are that heavenly earth which yielded its fruit. Heavenly Wisdom took you as the material from which it fashioned the temple of its body. The Holy Spirit filled you. The power of the Most High ineffably overshadowed you.

Carry my prayers to your Son, the Creator. Indeed, pray for me; plead for me, for your petitions cannot be despised, nor can your prayers be held cheap in his sight.

Behold, my Lady: unhappy me, caught in crime, am led to the gallows; a robber, to the sword; I am dragged away to punishment. Let the Queen of the world therefore arise, oppose herself, enter before her Son, and free the guilty man.

And come to my aid, O Michael, prince of the heavenly army. You who at the end of the world will slay the Antichrist, who insolently exalts himself against God, now cast down him who attempts to reign in my heart.

Free my soul from temptation while it lives in the body, so that after death you may be able worthily to present it to its Creator.

Help me also, blessed Gabriel, arranger of the heavenly marriage. Save by your prayers me, a miserable sinner, you who were sent to announce the one who was to come into the world to free sinners and the wretched (Luke I).

And heal my weakened soul, Saint Raphael, you who drove the demon from Sarah and restored to Tobias the eyes he had lost (Tobit III, XI). Exclude from my soul the evil spirit who attempts to separate her husband, Christ, from her, and pour the radiance of light into my blind heart.

Pray for me, all holy angels; all holy archangels; all holy virtues; all holy powers; all holy dominions; all holy principalities.

Pray for me, holy choir of thrones. Pray for me, holy choir of cherubim. Pray for me, holy choir of seraphim.

Pray for me, all holy patriarchs; all holy prophets.

Let the judging senate of the apostles pray for me.

Let the white-robed choir of martyrs pray for me.

Let all the holy confessors and all the holy virgins pray for me.

[Col. 0922A] Pray for me, miserable and utterly ruined, all you saints of God, my lords.

What multitude of sin could be so cruel that it could not be wiped away through the intercession of so many heavenly senators? For you cannot be empty of mercy, since you are inseparably united with mercy’s very fountain.

I know, Lord, that I do not deserve to touch the sacred thresholds of your church or raise my unhappy eyes to heaven. I am unworthy to utter your blessed and glorious name with my polluted and filthy lips.

But let your Spirit come, I beg, into my soul and wipe away all these impurities.

For if this sun, which is not among your higher creatures, has such power that it removes filth, illuminates the earth, and makes the fields fruitful, how much more will your Spirit, coeternal and consubstantial with you, deign to visit this unhappy little tree, already withering and stripped even of its leaves, and immediately make it green again! Nor will it lack the power to clothe it with the flowers of virtues and the beauty of fruits in springtime.

Come, Lord Jesus; come, sweet inhabitant within me. Your fragrance surpasses all spices; your sweetness surpasses honeycombs and every honey.

Come, I beg you, and claim me wholly as your possession, so that the tyrant may henceforth know that he has no part in me. Dedicate me entirely as your temple, because you are my God and Lord, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign forever and ever. Amen.

## III. Prayer to God the Holy Spirit

Holy Spirit, God almighty, coessential and coeternal with the supreme Father and the Son, proceeding ineffably from both, graciously pour yourself into my heart and, as a wondrous illuminator, drive away the darkness of my wickedness, so that, just as the womb of the Virgin was able, when you came upon it, to conceive the Word of God, I too may, through the assistance of your grace, always be able to carry in my mind the same Author of my salvation.

For you, Lord, are the light of minds; you are the strength of hearts; you are the life of souls.

You granted the holy apostles that they might fully understand the mysteries of human redemption and proclaim the rule of faith along the unimpeded path of truth.

You gave the blessed martyrs the boldness of holy freedom, so that they would fear neither the rulers of the world nor the carefully devised forms of punishment, but pass through them with the greatest steadfastness and endurance.

You spoke in the prophets; in the patriarchs you established the foundations of faith.

You gave all the saints both the will and the ability, and you bestowed on them all the flowers of virtue by which they might ascend to heaven.

And I, an unhappy sinner, how can I be saved without you, when without you I do not even recognize what I ought at least to pray for?

Certainly, Lord, if you depart, my soul does not live. For just as the body dies when the soul is withdrawn, so, when you depart, the soul itself must immediately be extinguished [Note: [Col. 0921D] That is, deprived of spiritual life.]

I feel it, I feel it, Lord: whenever your strength comes to me at some time through hidden grace, my spirit immediately grows strong. But when, because my sins demand it, you withdraw, my unhappy soul immediately dries up, wastes away, and collapses; nor does it rise to exercise itself in the practice of pure prayer.

Descend, therefore, into me, eternal giver of life, and kindle the ice of my breast with the flame of your charity.

Give water to my head and dissolve the stony hardness of my heart. Upon this element, Lord, you were borne even before the origin of the world (Genesis I); and now you descend for the purification of souls into the life-giving streams of the fountain.

Come, therefore, into me with the water of compunction, and give me drink in measured tears.

Woe to me, miserable sinner, who commit innumerable things each day that ought to be mourned, and yet cannot weep!

Let the rain of your grace, Lord, therefore fall upon me, so that my soul, which had dried up by withdrawing from the fountain of life, may bloom anew through the breath of your visitation.

My heart is ready; my heart is ready.

Behold, Lord, I open to you all the recesses of my heart; I loosen the secrets of my breast and eagerly await the approach of your gracious favor.

Certainly the eye of the flesh has its own light, namely the visible sun; but my inner self awaits you, who are the light of souls. You who illumined the man blind from birth (John 9), illumine me. You who raised Lazarus (John 11), give me life. Alas, alas, unhappy soul: although you are the life of the body, lying there yourself dead, you do not deserve to have your life-giver as your Spirit. Dead to yourself, you live for another; and, established in darkness yourself, you grant light to the outward substance. Yet you cannot see, because you do not possess your own light.

Come, I beseech you, Spirit of truth, and powerfully drive all the darkness of error from me. Judge, Lord, those who harm me, and [Col. 0923C] overthrow those who attack me; take up arms and shield, and rise to my aid (Psalm 34). You, Spirit who purify and give life, almighty eternal God, are a consuming fire. You are the Spirit of judgment, you the Spirit of burning. Therefore scour my heart, wipe away by the power of your burning all the rust of faults and vices, and wholly exclude from all my senses the spirit of wickedness hostile to you.

Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his face. As smoke vanishes, so let them vanish; as wax melts before the fire, so let sinners perish before the face of God (Psalm 67). Come, I beg you, come, blessed Spirit of truth, and enter as the innermost searcher into all the veins of my inward being. Take away whatever is fermented, whatever is vicious, whatever you find corrupted by the pestilence of harmful antiquity; [Col. 0923D] make me unleavened and sincere through the purity of your cleansing.

Restore me dead to myself and alive to you. Mortify in me every source of carnal pleasures, refine me completely, and make me wholly extinguished not only to vices but also to the world. Come, I beseech you, Spirit of eternal blessing, and flood every hiding place of my breast with the ineffable sweetness of your delight. Let my soul melt at your coming; renewed through you, let it conceive heavenly strength. Let it return to the source of its vigor and burn with kindled inward parts in love of you.

Bless the Lord, my soul, and all that is within me, his holy name (Psalm 102). May my soul receive the abundant blessing of your grace, Lord; and, so that it may offer you [Col. 0924A] sacrifices from the marrow, may it grow rich, fattened by the fatness of your ineffable sweetness. Illumine me, light of truth; kindle me; purify me. For you are the giver of spiritual gifts, the author of sanctification, and the remission of all sins. You continually inflame the angelic powers with love of you; the cherubim and seraphim burn incomparably in the fire of your charity.

Claim me wholly for yourself, Lord; possess me wholly, and permit no part of me to remain empty of you. Rather, live alone in me, and make me live for you alone, who live and are glorified in perfect Trinity, one true God, for ever and ever. Amen.

## IV. Prayers to the Holy Trinity

I adore you, I worship you, I glorify you, I magnify you, blessed, [Col. 0924B] almighty Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, three and one God. Help me, Lord; absolve me, purify me, cleanse me, my King and my God. Give me justice, fortitude, temperance, and prudence. Give me perfect faith, hope, and charity. Grant me the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and fortitude, of knowledge and piety, and of your fear. Give me the lower and the upper pool. Give me blessing from the dew of heaven and from the richness of the earth. Soften, Lord, my heart of stone. Give me compunction and contrition of heart, so that I may mourn my countless sins.

Lord, I am not worthy to enter your church. I am unworthy to raise my unhappy eyes to heaven or to utter your blessed name [Col. 0924C] with my lips; but you, who created me as you will and as you know, have mercy on me, Lord my God.

## V. Second prayer

Have mercy, Lord, on all my friends and relatives, on all my benefactors, on all who pray to you for me, and on all who ask me to pray for them. Give them fruitful repentance; mortify in them every vice, and make them flourish in your virtues. Make them, Lord, live in every respect so that by their good conduct they may be able to please your majesty.

Have mercy, God, on bishops, kings, authorities, and all the Christian people. Holy Mary, pray for them all. All holy men and women of God, pray for them. Have mercy, Lord, [Col. 0924D] on all my deceased benefactors and on all for whom I am bound to pray; absolve all your faithful and grant them a share and fellowship with your saints. Holy Virgin Mary, pray for all; all holy men and women of God, pray for them all.

## VI. Third prayer

I adore you, one in Trinity and three in unity, blessed, almighty Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Have mercy on me, a most wretched sinner, most merciful my God, and have mercy on all your faithful, living and dead.

Holy Virgin Mary, mother of God and of humankind, temple of the living God, virgin before childbirth and virgin after childbirth, exalted above the choirs [Col. 0925A] of angels, pray for us all.

Holy Michael, prince of the heavenly host; holy Gabriel, mediator of the heavenly nuptials; holy Raphael, medicine of God: pray for us. Saint John the Baptist, pray for us. Saint Peter, who holds the keys of the kingdom of heaven; Saint Paul; Saint Andrew; Saint John the Evangelist: pray for us all. Saint Stephen, Saint Apollinaris, Saint Lawrence: pray for us all. Saint Sylvester, Saint Martin, Saint Benedict, our venerable father: pray for us all. Saint Agatha, Saint Agnes, Saint Cecilia: pray for us all.

All holy angels and archangels, thrones and dominions, principalities, powers, virtues, cherubim and seraphim; all holy patriarchs and prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, virgins, hermits, widows; all [Col. 0925B] holy men and women of God: pray for us all, Christ’s faithful, living and dead.

Our Father.

## VII. Also, prayers concerning the Holy Trinity

God, by whose gift we confess both Trinity in persons and unity in the divine substance, graciously grant that, armed with this breastplate of faith, we may deserve to be delivered from every adversity. Through the Lord.

## VIII. Another

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who confess one essence of the Holy Trinity may, just as now we walk by faith with you as our guide, one day, with you as our receiver, be brought to the vision. Through him.

## IX. Another

[Col. 0925C] God, who have taught us to believe both the Trinity without confusion and the substance of your majesty without division, grant to your suppliants that upon this foundation of the catholic faith the structure of holy virtues may rise within us. Through the Lord.

## X. Another

God, who have revealed to us the mystery of the Holy Trinity, grant, we beseech you, that we who already live by faith may grow through the increase of good works. Through our Lord.

## XI. On the Annunciation of the Lord

Behold, the herald of the King prepares the closed palace.

## XII. On the Nativity of the Lord

He who was born from eternity comes forth from the Virgin’s womb.

## XIII. On the Presentation of the Lord

[Col. 0925D] He whom the heavens cannot contain, Simeon holds in his arms.

## XIV. On the Baptism of the Lord

Behold, the river washes the pure spring; O Jordan, wash the one who washes you, from whom you yourself are more greatly cleansed.

## XV. On the Transfiguration of the Lord

Here God displays what he concealed beneath the covering of flesh.

## XVI. When the children say “Hosanna” (“save, we pray”)

The stars, the heavens, and the earth fear him whom the she-ass carries.

With a great voice the assembly proclaims “Hosanna” (“save, we pray”) to God.

## XVII. On the Lord’s Supper

He who is head washes the feet of his righteous disciples.

What he forbade to one party, Peter wishes to undo for all.

## XVIII. On the paten

[Col. 0926A]

These dishes produce food of everlasting life.

## XIX. When Judas betrays the Lord

The fierce false wolf extends flattering kisses to the Lamb.

## XX. When Christ prays to the Father

You pray to the Father, Christ, with whom together you grant all things.

## XXI. The Lord says to his disciples: “Watch”

The King of the watchful ordered those whom sleep had overcome to rise.

## XXII and XXIII. Prayers to be said on Good Friday during the adoration of the cross

[Note: [Col. 0925] The prayer of the first genuflection, as well as part of the second, is missing in the manuscript.]

[lacuna] the one struck might look toward him and escape the deadly poison, and might attain the life of the hoped-for salvation, signifying that you yourself, in ages far afterward, would be raised up on the scaffold of the cross for the salvation of your creature, so that those whom the devil had taken captive with the weapons of envy might be recalled to their homeland by your desirable passion.

Grant both to me, wretched and sinful, and to all those purchased by your blood, who today devoutly venerate your holy passion and adore the wood of life, that with your help we may overcome the devil’s snares and deserve to become participants in eternal life, you who live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

## XXIV. At the third genuflection

Lord Jesus Christ, who today, through the passion of your holy cross, freed us from the devil’s servitude, so that on the same day on which you formed humankind you might also restore it: hear me, wretched and sinful, confessing and praying before this sign of your holy cross. Grant that, protected by the defense of this venerable and life-giving sign, [Col. 0926C] I may be able both to repel the fiery darts of the most wicked enemy and to be freed from the wounds inflicted upon me, and to reach eternal life, through you, Lord Jesus Christ, who live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

## XXV. Other prayers concerning the Holy Cross

While I adore the cross of your most beloved Son, almighty Father, may heaven be opened to me, I beseech you, so that my prayer may reach you and your mercy may descend upon me. For this singular victim, most loving Lord, offered to you as a sweet-smelling fragrance, both appeases your justice toward us and, like the burning of pious incense evaporating from the censer of the most sacred passion, sweetens the nostrils of human minds.

O indescribable victim, which both abolished the guarantee of the ancient curse [Col. 0926D] and impressed upon us the seal of eternal blessing. O sacrifice of true reconciliation and praise, which both removed the enmity of the ancient transgression and restored between heaven and earth a covenant of eternal peace.

By this, Lord, the distinguished banner of your power, rescue me, the wretched little sheep of your flock, from the jaws of the bloodstained lion, so that, defeated and crushed by you, he may not be able to triumph over me. Lead me back to the ever-green and pleasant pastures of your own, and do not cast away the servant for whom you deigned to surrender your Son, who with you and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God for ever and ever. Amen.

## XXVI. Prayer

[Col. 0927A]

Mediator of God and humankind, Lord Jesus Christ, who assumed true flesh from the undefiled womb of blessed Mary, and who offered to God the Father upon the altar of the cross, as a sweet-smelling fragrance, the Lamb of your immaculate body for our salvation, and who made yourself medicine for the human race so that it might vomit out the poison of the ancient transgression: absolve me, exceedingly unhappy and miserable, bound by countless chains of sins.

Behold, Lord, before the very banner of your life-giving cross I prostrate myself, and as a suppliant I adore the new and unheard-of triumph of your victory. For you are both priest and victim; you are both redeemer and price.

It pleases me, most loving Lord, to see you hanging on the punishment of the cross as though at the very moment of your recent passion. It pleases me to receive in my mouth the most precious blood dripping down.

O truly blessed victim, which both breaks through the walls of Tartarus and opens the gate of the heavenly kingdom to the faithful. O weight of our price, weighed on the balance of the cross, by which the ancient creditor laments that the written bond of our debt has been cut away.

I see you with the eyes within, my Redeemer, fastened with the nails of the cross. I see you wounded with new wounds. I hear you saying to the thief in a clear voice: “Today you will be with me in paradise” (Luke 23).

Therefore, through the mystery of this your saving passion and death I implore you; through this sacrament of our redemption, I say, I tearfully beseech you. Do not, as I deserve, separate me from the fellowship of your elect, but establish me in the glory of paradise with that blessed thief himself.

[Col. 0927C] Lord, mark my soul with the imprint of this holy cross; purify me by its power. Through it claim me wholly, on every side, for your jurisdiction, so that no portion of the adversary may be found in me at all. Thus, when you come for judgment, when this insignia of divine power shines in heaven, may I be found marked with this stigma, so that, conformed to the crucified one in punishment, I may deserve to become a partner of the risen one in glory, you who live and reign with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit for ever and ever. Amen.

## XXVII. Prayer

If I knew that your mercy, most gentle God, had human measure, I, crushed beneath so enormous a mass of crimes, would despair utterly. But while I see so powerful a victim being sacrificed for me, I do not consider how I ought to despair.

For if that paschal lamb, a mere brute animal, could free the people of Israel from the plague of death (Exodus 12), how much more can the most sacred blood of him who is the Creator of angels wash away whatever filth there may be in my soul?

You, most loving Lord Jesus Christ, give off fragrance like an aromatic spice crushed in the mortar of your passion [Col. 0927D], so that you might become medicine for us wretched people languishing from the sickness of sins. You were trampled in the press of the cross like that cluster of the land flowing with milk and honey (Numbers 13), so that you might offer us the cup of eternal salvation and flood our parched hearts with the inundation of the Holy Spirit.

Lord, through the five wounds of your most sacred body you healed all the wounds inflicted upon us through the five senses of our body. [Col. 0928A] You became for the Father a sacrifice of sweetness and for us the price of redemption.

I adore your cross, Lord; I adore your life-giving death. May your blood, I beseech you, wash away the filth of my soul, and may the creditor no longer hold liable the one for whom so sublime a price has been paid.

May this title of your victory, Lord, always stand erect in my soul, so that no ancient invader may claim any right over your possession. When he sees this, may he flee at once and vanish like smoke at the approach of your Spirit. May you deign through continual grace to possess your inheritance, which you purchased with your own blood; and by your mercy may you be both its unconquered protector and its constant inhabitant, you who with God the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

## XXVIII. Prayer

[Col. 0928B]

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, we give thanks to your immeasurable mercy: although you were in the form of God, you humbled yourself for us, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross.

We beseech you, Lord, to grant true forgiveness of sins to those to whom you have bestowed such great grace. Preserve in us the works of your mercy, lest those whom your right hand redeemed perish. Heal the sicknesses of your people and give glory to your name.

I also ask you, most loving Lord, not to reject me, miserable and fragile, from your grace; and although I have until now departed far from your will, corrupted, may I henceforth, corrected by your ineffable mercy, happily please your majesty.

Drive from me, Lord, whatever is harmful, whatever is unsuitable, whatever is vicious, whatever is contrary to your will. [Col. 0928C] Grant me, Lord, to mourn my evils worthily here while I live, and may my repentance be acceptable in your sight. Grant me true faith, firm hope, and sincere charity. Let humility, a sober life, true knowledge, fortitude, prudence, justice, temperance, a straight course, and a perfect end be fixed in me, with you as our provider, our God, who with the Father, and so forth.

## XXIX. Prayer

[Col. 0928D]

Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth, king of angels and of all the saints, who before the ages were the only-begotten Son with God the Father in the essence of divinity; but in the fullness of time, emptying yourself, you received from the Virgin Mary the form of a servant’s body, becoming in the likeness of a human being and being found in appearance as a human being.

Assuming a true human being into the true God, humbled and made obedient unto death, even death on a cross, you redeemed us by your holy and precious blood. The immaculate Lamb, rising from the dead and ascending into heaven, you sit at the right hand of God the almighty Father.

The angels adore you, and I, unhappy sinner, devoutly adore you, confessing my sins and beseeching you that, just as you made me a participant through the cross in the sacraments of your death and redemption, so through the power of this most holy cross you may extinguish and destroy in me all vices and sins, and, by invoking the power of that same most holy cross against all spiritual wickedness and the snares of the ancient enemy, make victorious weapons for me.

Grant that, rising with you in newness of spirit and glory, I may reach [Col. 0929A] the things that are above, with your saints and elect placed at your right hand—you, the same Jesus Christ, immortal God, who live and reign with God the Father and the Holy Spirit for endless ages of ages. Amen.

## XXX. Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, most glorious Creator of the world, who, being the radiance of glory, coeternal and equal with the Father and the Holy Spirit, deigned for this reason to take immaculate flesh from the Virgin and permitted your innocent and glorious hands to be fastened to the scaffold of the cross, so that you might shatter the gates of hell and free the human race from death: have mercy [Col. 0929B] on me, wretched, oppressed by the heavy burden of many crimes and polluted by the filth of many wickednesses.

Do not abandon me, most loving Lord, but mercifully forgive what I have done wickedly and what I have done negligently. Hear me, I beseech you, most merciful and compassionate Jesus, good and gracious God, prostrate before your most glorious cross, which must be adored, so that during these holy days and always I may deserve to stand before you clean and continually please your sight. Thus, freed from every evil, may I always be consoled by your help, Christ the Lord, Savior of the world, who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

## XXXI. Prayer

Christ, who underwent the scaffold of the cross and death for us [Col. 0929C] in order to drive the power of death from us and free us by the price of your blood, have mercy on me, your most humble servant, and grant me forgiveness for all my sins. As I prostrate myself before your cross, which must be adored, rescue me during these holy days and always from every evil, and mercifully refresh me with your goods, you who with God the Father and the Holy Spirit live and reign through immeasurable ages of ages. Amen.

## XXXII. Prayer

God, who restored to something better through the wood the human being who had perished through wood, we beseech you: may the power of this triumphant wood, enriched by your death and blood, to which we submit our necks with complete devotion, both mortify every vice in us and protect us against every adversity, you who live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever.

## XXXIII. Prayer

Lord Jesus Christ, who are and who were God, begotten with the Father before the ages, God from true God, conceived from the Holy Spirit and born as a human being at the end of the ages from the ever-virgin Mary; obedient to the Father unto death, even death on a cross, you redeemed us by your holy and precious blood, and, having destroyed the dominion of death, opened the entrance to heavenly glory for all who believe in you.

I devoutly adore you as true God and my Lord, sitting at the right hand of God the almighty Father, beseeching your infinite and ineffable mercy. Through the power of this saving sign of our redemption, redeem me, wretched sinner worthy of death, from all my crimes and misdeeds; free me from all past, present, and future evils; mortify in me every vice of spiritual and carnal wickedness; make me rise in the power of your grace and glory; make me desire and seek the things above, the heavenly things; and grant that I may happily attain the glory of eternal blessedness.

This grant through your immeasurable clemency, Lord Jesus Christ, our God and Lord, who with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, in the unity of the Godhead, rule all things by creating, give them life, and govern them through immortal ages of ages. Amen.

## XXXIV. Litany

[Col. 0930B]

Christ, hear us, three times.

Father in heaven, God, have mercy on us.

Son, Redeemer of the world, God, have mercy on us.

Holy Spirit, God, have mercy on us.

Holy Trinity, one God, have mercy on us.

Holy Mother of God, ever undefiled, Virgin Mary, and all holy seraphim and cherubim, intercede for us and for all the faithful, living and dead . . . .

## XXXV. Hymn on the Holy Cross. At Matins

Cross, salvation of the lost world,

life of the world destroyed,

before you the conquered realms of Tartarus tremble,

the hosts of heaven stand in awe of you.

While life dies in you,

[Col. 0930C] the chain of death is loosed;

freed from the yoke of Egypt,

we are children of the true light.

The Judge of all places his throne upon you

when he is judged;

even then he separates the goats

from the sheep among the thieves.

You make sport of the prince of the world

while you punish the impassible One;

accustomed to offer up the guilty,

you now give him, and he carries off spoils.

Upon you the victim is slain

which cleanses the crimes of the world;

to you the talent is entrusted

which cancels Adam’s debt.

[Col. 0930D]

Protect us, sign of life,

whom the King of glory triumphs;

through you may he advance to the kingdom

those whom he frees from servitude.

Praise be to the unbegotten Father;

honor to the Only-begotten;

may supreme majesty be to the equal Spirit

of both.

## XXXVI. At Lauds

Cross, blessing of the world,

hope and certain redemption,

once the bearer of Gehenna,

now the bright gate of heaven.

Upon you the victim is lifted,

the one who drew all things to himself;

the prince of the world attacks him

and finds nothing that belongs to him.

The article of your law

cancels the ancient written bond;

ancient servitude perishes,

true freedom is restored.

The abundance of your fragrance

surpasses all spices;

the sweetness of your nectar

fills the hidden places of the breast.

[Col. 0931A]

Through the cross, Christ, we beseech you,

transfer to the reward of life

those whom, fixed to the trunk of the wood,

you deigned to redeem.

[Col. 0931B]

Praise be to the unbegotten Father;

honor to the Only-begotten;

may supreme majesty be to the equal Spirit

of both.

## XXXVII. Consolatory hymn on the Holy Cross

Unique hope of humankind, O venerable sign of the cross,

be salvation for all, unique hope of humankind.

You bear the price by which the debts of the world are cancelled;

the price by which it deserved to be redeemed, you bear the price.

Unique hope of humankind, O venerable sign of the cross,

be salvation for all, unique hope of humankind.

Tartarus, conquered by your triumphs, surrendered its spoils;

Tartarus, conquered by your standards, mourns.

You open the stars to the pious, whom you mark with your own stigma;

you give rest to the weary, you open the stars to the pious.

[Col. 0931C]

Unique hope of humankind, O venerable sign of the cross,

be salvation for all, unique hope of humankind.

The written bond which the guarantee of the forbidden wood had drawn up,

you erase—the written bond of the forbidden fruit.

Light, honor, dominion, praise, glory, *doxa* (glory), through the ages:

be yours, triune God, light, honor, dominion.

Unique hope of humankind, O venerable sign of the cross,

be salvation for all, unique hope of humankind.

## XXXVIII. On the Holy Cross

This fearsome figure is one hope for all;

behold the price hanging balanced on the scales,

which redeems the world and cancels the debt of the first-formed man.

The cross is life to me; O enemy, it is death to you.

## XXXIX. Also, on the Holy Cross, for two enemies reconciled to each other

Behold, the cross of Christ reddens, stained with fresh blood;

[Col. 0931D] it joins heaven with earth, the lowest with the highest.

It commands that the light of love arise among you;

when quarrels have been settled, let kisses of peace follow.

## XL. Easter hymn

The joy of the Paschal feast

fills the world’s expanse;

let heaven, earth, and seas

joyfully utter songs,

and let them sing “Alleluia” (“Praise the Lord”)

with harmonious instruments.

Let Tartarus alone howl,

empty of its stolen prey;

let it mourn its broken bars

and its iron walls laid low,

[Col. 0932A] which the King of glory overthrew

with the praise of victory.

Wonderful is the law of the mystery,

a new kind of battle:

the bound one frees those bound;

the dead gives life.

While life itself is slain,

it becomes the death of death.

The balance of the cross weighs

the price of the world;

while the creditor demanded it,

he lost his ancient right.

He tries to swallow the bait,

but is pierced by the hook.

The first-formed man drew up

the written bond of humankind;

Christ afterward cancelled it

on another tablet of wood.

What the first Adam had written,

the second effaces.

When the Author of life dies,

the world also dies with him;

the sun covered its rays;

the mourning earth trembled;

the veil of the temple was torn,

the strength of the rocks was split.

[Col. 0932B]

He whom heaven cannot contain

is enclosed in a brief tomb.

Surrounded by rich spoil,

after the prince of death was conquered,

[Col. 0932C] triumphant power

rises on the third day.

Give Christ back, guards,

whom you soldiers guarded,

or show him dead,

or believe that he is alive.

Why do you freely proclaim the truth

while, having been paid, you invent falsehoods?

Soon the angelic message resounds

to the women,

so that they might bring these sweet tidings

to the apostles:

“Go to Galilee;

there you will see Christ.”

Now, freed from the servitude

[Col. 0932D] of the Egyptian king,

after crossing the Red Sea,

let us give a new song;

released from the laws of death,

we have risen with Christ.

Honor, peoples newly born,

rightly the Lord’s Passover;

stain the doorposts of your houses

with the blood of the Paschal Lamb;

drive out the old leaven,

eat unleavened bread.

With all our inward being,

Christ, we return praises to you:

you who, rising from the dead,

no longer die.

[Col. 0933A]

Praise be to the Father and all honor

to the equal Spirit. Amen.

## XLI. On the Ascension of the Lord

God sought the depths, but did not leave the heights;

he is where he goes, and remains whence he came.

## XLII. Hymn on the Ascension of the Lord. At Lauds

Let the bright summits of the heavens

gaze with joyful lights

upon the King of glory,

who enters with the triumph of victory.

He who had come to die,

death having been destroyed, returns,

a noble victor to the stars,

carrying away the spoils of Gehenna.

[Col. 0933B]

That he might raise up the fallen,

that he might redeem the sold,

he brings back to the pastures

the sheep that had strayed after spurning the pastures.

Now, flesh, despise the mud;

enter heaven, O earth:

for a path is laid through the limbs

where you see the head go.

Jesus, glory of angels,

sweetness and desire,

make us also, we beseech you,

embrace you with all our inward being.

Grant us to live in you;

direct our heart toward you;

may your love kindle our breasts

[Col. 0933C] for ever.

## XLIII. When the Holy Spirit descends upon the apostles

The flame of tongues kindles the apostolic senate,

and a fruitful voice produces varied forms of speech.

## XLIV. On the Annunciation of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary. Hymn. At Matins

Let all earthly things rejoice;

let the stars resound with praises;

before the Virgin’s bridal chamber

let them alternate hymns of praise [*dragmatum*: the reading is uncertain].

This Virgin, pregnant with the Word,

becomes the gate of paradise;

she who returned God to the world

opened heaven to us.

Happy is this mother,

freed from Eve’s sentence;

she conceived without a man,

she gave birth without a groan.

Mary’s rich womb

carried the price of the world,

by which we glory in being redeemed,

released from the yoke of debt.

The Son of the Father fills her;

the Holy Spirit overshadows her;

the most chaste inward parts

of the sacred maiden become heaven.

Praise be to you, Most High,

who were born from the Virgin;

honor be to the ineffable Father

and to the holy Spirit. Amen.

## XLV. At Lauds

[Col. 0934A]

Like a radiant dawn,

she journeys to the heights of heaven,

bright as the sun, Mary,

most beautiful like the moon.

Today the Queen of the world

ascends the throne of glory,

having borne that Son

who existed before Lucifer.

[Col. 0934B]

Taken above the angels,

she surpasses the archangels;

this one woman alone

transcends all the merits of the saints.

The one whom she had warmed in her lap,

whom she had laid in a manger,

now she sees as King over all,

in the glory of the Father.

For us, Virgin of virgins,

ask your Son;

through you he had assumed our nature,

so that he might grant us his.

Praise be to you, Most High,

who were born from the Virgin;

honor be to the ineffable Father

and to the holy Spirit. Amen.

## XLVI. In the same Annunciation of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary. At Mass, Preface

Through Christ our Lord. On this day, through the message of the archangel Gabriel, he disclosed to the undefiled Mother, full of grace, the mystery of his saving advent; and, conceived in the flower of a flourishing womb, he turned the old leaven into unleavened bread, because, taking on a human being, he did not contract the contagion of the original corruption of human nature.

Indeed, he fashioned for himself a breastplate from our weakness; in it, rejoicing like a giant and powerful and strong in battle, he defeated the aerial powers. He covered himself with the veil of weak flesh, although he was almighty in the majesty of his everlasting essence. And while the Word of the Father united himself to human nature, the heavenly Bridegroom joined the holy Church to himself in the bridal chamber of the virgin womb—for whose love he did not disdain the confinements of the maternal womb, although he cannot be contained by the infinite breadth of heaven.

Whom the angels praise.

## XLVII. On the Assumption of that Most Holy Virgin. Hymn at Vespers

[Col. 0934D]

Joy of the world, new star of heaven,

giving birth to the Sun, bearing the Father,

give your hands to the fallen, bring help to the failing,

Virgin Mary.

It is evident that you are God’s ladder,

which, holding the highest, reaches down to the lowest;

grant us to return to the heights

of exalted heaven.

The choir of blessed angels,

the holy prophets, and the order of apostles

see you, one woman, placed above them

after the Godhead.

The splendid court of the heavenly King,

supported by the seven columns of wisdom:

[Col. 0935A] him whom the whole world cannot contain

you enclose in your womb.

Him whom the heavens tremble at, whom the abysses fear,

the drops of rivers and the storms of the sea,

the setting sun praises and the rising sun venerates—

you hold in your arms.

The food of angels is nourished by milk;

he is carried in the lap of an unmarried maiden,

he who by his broad dominion

weighs the burdens of the earth.

[Col. 0935B]

Thus may there be honor without end to Christ Most High,

whom holy Mary the Virgin bore,
